questions.question: P starts a business with Rs. 8,000. Q joins after 5 months with Rs. 12,000. If the profit at the end of the year is Rs. 6,800, what is Q's share (approx.)?
questions.questionHtml: P starts a business with Rs. 8,000. Q joins after 5 months with Rs. 12,000. If the profit at the end of the year is Rs. 6,800, what is Q's share (approx.)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Profit ratio = (Capital1 × Time1) : (Capital2 × Time2)

Ratio (P : Q) = (8000 × 12) : (12000 × 7)

Ratio (P : Q) = 96000 : 84000 = 8 : 7

Total profit ratio parts = 8 + 7 = 15 parts

Q's share = (7 / 15) × 6800 ≈ Rs. 3173.33

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3173.33.

Alternate Method

Given:

P's initial investment = Rs. 8,000

Investment duration for P = 12 months

Q's joining investment = Rs. 12,000

Investment duration for Q = 12 − 5 = 7 months

Total annual profit = Rs. 6,800

Formula Used:

Profit Ratio = (Capital of A × Time of A) : (Capital of B × Time of B)

Calculations:

⇒ Profit ratio of P to Q = (8000 × 12) : (12000 × 7)

⇒ Profit ratio = 96000 : 84000

⇒ Profit ratio = 96 : 84

Dividing the ratio by 12:

⇒ Profit ratio (P : Q) = 8 : 7

⇒ Total profit units = 8 + 7 = 15 units

⇒ Q's share in profit = (7 / 15) × Total Profit

⇒ Q's share = (7 / 15) × 6800

⇒ Q's share = 47600 / 15

⇒ Q's share = 3173.33

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3173.33.

Additional Information

Compound Partnership

When partners invest different capital amounts for different time periods, the profit is divided in the ratio of the product of their capital and time: Profit Ratio = C1T1 : C2T2.

Joining Mid-Way

If a business profit is evaluated annually (12 months) and a partner joins after 't' months, their active period for generating profit is calculated as (12 − t) months.

Sleeping Partner vs Active Partner

An active partner manages the business and usually receives a fixed salary or a specific percentage of profit prior to general division. A sleeping partner only invests capital and receives profit strictly according to the investment ratio.

questions.question: A trapezoid is formed by cutting a smaller triangle from the top of a larger similar triangle. If the height of the smaller triangle is \(\frac{1}{3}\) of the height of the larger triangle, what is the ratio of the area of the trapezoid to the area of the larger triangle?
questions.questionHtml: A trapezoid is formed by cutting a smaller triangle from the top of a larger similar triangle. If the height of the smaller triangle is \(\frac{1}{3}\) of the height of the larger triangle, what is the ratio of the area of the trapezoid to the area of the larger triangle?
questions.solution:
Height ratio (smaller : larger) = 1 : 3

⇒ Side ratio (smaller : larger) = 1 ÷ 3

⇒ Area ratio (smaller : larger) = (1 ÷ 3)2 = 1 ÷ 9

⇒ Area of trapezoid = 1 − 1 ÷ 9 = 8 ÷ 9

⇒ Required ratio = 8 : 9

questions.question: If sin A = 8/17 and cos B = 15/17,find sin A cos B+cosA sinB:
questions.questionHtml: If sin A = 8/17 and  cos B = 15/17,find sin A cos B+cosA sinB:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The expression sin A cos B + cos A sin B follows the compound angle identity sin(A + B).

Given sin A = 8/17 and cos B = 15/17, notice they belong to the Pythagorean triplet (8, 15, 17).

This implies cos A = 15/17 and sin B = 8/17 as they share the same hypotenuse 17.

Substituting values: (8/17 × 15/17) + (15/17 × 8/17) = 120/289 + 120/289 = 240/289.

∴ The correct answer is 240/289.

Alternate Method

Given: sin A = 8/17 and cos B = 15/17

Formula Used: sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B | cos2θ = 1 − sin2θ

⇒ First, find cos A: cos A = √(1 − sin2 A) = √(1 − (8/17)2)

⇒ cos A = √(1 − 64/289) = √(225/289) = 15/17

⇒ Next, find sin B: sin B = √(1 − cos2 B) = √(1 − (15/17)2)

⇒ sin B = √(1 − 225/289) = √(64/289) = 8/17

⇒ Required value = (8/17 × 15/17) + (15/17 × 8/17)

⇒ Value = 120/289 + 120/289 = 240/289

∴ The correct answer is 240/289.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Identities for Sum/Difference

sin(A ± B) = sin A cos B ± cos A sin B and cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B.

Pythagorean Triplets

Sets of three positive integers a, b, and c such that a2 + b2 = c2. Common examples include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17).

Range of Sine and Cosine

For any real angle θ, −1 ≤ sin θ ≤ 1 and −1 ≤ cos θ ≤ 1.

questions.question: A circle has a radius of 13 cm. A chord is drawn at a distance of 5 cm from the center. What is the length of the chord?
questions.questionHtml: A circle has a radius of 13 cm. A chord is drawn at a distance of 5 cm from the center. What is the length of the chord?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In a circle, the radius, the perpendicular distance to the chord, and half the chord always form a right-angled triangle.

We can directly use the standard Pythagorean triplet (5, 12, 13).

Since the hypotenuse (radius) is 13 cm and one side is 5 cm, the other side (half the chord) must be 12 cm.

Length of the full chord = 2 × 12 cm = 24 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of the circle (OA) = 13 cm

Perpendicular distance from the center to the chord (OM) = 5 cm

Formula Used:

According to Pythagoras theorem: Hypotenuse2 = Base2 + Perpendicular2

The perpendicular drawn from the center of a circle to a chord bisects the chord.

Calculations:

In right-angled triangle OMA:

⇒ OA2 = OM2 + AM2

⇒ 132 = 52 + AM2

⇒ 169 = 25 + AM2

⇒ AM2 = 169 − 25

⇒ AM2 = 144

⇒ AM = √144 = 12 cm

Since the perpendicular from the center bisects the chord, full chord AB = 2 × AM

⇒ Length of chord AB = 2 × 12 = 24 cm

∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.

Additional Information

Perpendicular from Center to Chord

A perpendicular drawn from the center of a circle to any chord bisects the chord into two equal halves.

Common Pythagorean Triplets

Memorizing integer sets that satisfy a2 + b2 = c2 saves critical calculation time. Important triplets include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25) along with their multiples.

Intersecting Chords Theorem

If two chords AB and CD intersect internally at point P, then the products of their segments are always equal: PA × PB = PC × PD.

Angle in a Semicircle

The angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference of a circle is exactly 90°.

questions.question: The average of 5 consecutive odd natural numbers is 27. Previous 5 consecutive odd natural numbers to these 5 odd natural numbers are also included. What will be the average of newly added numbers?
questions.questionHtml: The average of 5 consecutive odd natural numbers is 27. Previous 5 consecutive odd natural numbers to these 5 odd natural numbers are also included. What will be the average of newly added numbers?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The average of 5 consecutive odd numbers is always the middle term.

Middle term of original set = 27.

The previous set also contains 5 consecutive odd numbers.

Since both sets have 5 terms, the difference between their averages is 2 × 5 = 10.

Average of new numbers = 27 − 10 = 17.

∴ The correct answer is 17.

Alternate Method

Given: Average of 5 consecutive odd natural numbers = 27.

Calculations:

⇒ Let the 5 consecutive odd numbers be: (x − 4), (x − 2), x, (x + 2), (x + 4)

⇒ Average = Sum ÷ 5 = [ (x−4) + (x−2) + x + (x+2) + (x+4) ] ÷ 5 = 5x ÷ 5 = x

⇒ Given average = 27, so x = 27.

⇒ Original numbers are: 23, 25, 27, 29, 31.

⇒ The 5 consecutive odd numbers previous to these are: 13, 15, 17, 19, 21.

⇒ Average of these newly added numbers = (13 + 15 + 17 + 19 + 21) ÷ 5 = 85 ÷ 5 = 17.

∴ The correct answer is 17.

Additional Information

Average of Arithmetic Progression

For any consecutive numbers (AP), the average is always (First term + Last term) ÷ 2 or the middle term if the count is odd.

Consecutive Odd/Even Numbers

In a sequence of consecutive odd or even numbers, the common difference between any two successive terms is always 2.

Shift in Average

If every number in a data set is increased or decreased by a constant value 'k', the average also increases or decreases by exactly 'k'.

questions.question: A regular right triangular pyramid has base side = 10 cm, and slant height = 13 cm. Find the total surface area if all slant heights are equal and the base is equilateral.
questions.questionHtml: A regular right triangular pyramid has base side = 10 cm, and slant height = 13 cm. Find the total surface area if all slant heights are equal and the base is equilateral.

options.html: 282.7 cm2
300.5 cm2
320.3 cm2

questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Lateral Surface Area (LSA) = (1/2) × Perimeter × Slant height = (1/2) × 30 × 13 = 195 cm2.

Base Area = (√3 / 4) × 102 ≈ 0.433 × 100 = 43.3 cm2.

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 195 + 43.3 = 238.3 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 238.3 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Base side (a) of the equilateral triangle = 10 cm

Slant height (l) of the pyramid = 13 cm

Formula Used:

Total Surface Area (TSA) = Lateral Surface Area (LSA) + Base Area

LSA = (1/2) × Perimeter of base × Slant height

Base Area = (√3 / 4) × a2

Calculations:

⇒ Perimeter of the base = 3 × 10 = 30 cm

⇒ Lateral Surface Area = (1/2) × 30 × 13 = 195 cm2

⇒ Base Area = (√3 / 4) × 102

⇒ Base Area = (1.732 / 4) × 100 = 0.433 × 100 = 43.3 cm2

⇒ Total Surface Area = 195 + 43.3 = 238.3 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 238.3 cm2.

Additional Information

Volume of a Pyramid

The volume (V) of any pyramid is given by V = (1/3) × Base Area × Vertical Height (h).

Slant Height vs. Slant Edge

Slant height (l) is the altitude of the lateral triangular face, whereas slant edge (e) is the distance from the apex to a base vertex.

Pythagorean Relation in Pyramids

For a regular pyramid, l2 = h2 + r2, where r is the in-radius of the base, and e2 = h2 + R2, where R is the circum-radius.

questions.question: If sin A = 3/5, and A is acute, find the value of sec 2 A - tan 2 A.
questions.questionHtml: If sin A = 3/5, and A is acute, find the value of sec2 A - tan2 A.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The expression sec2A − tan2A is a fundamental trigonometric identity.

By identity, for any angle A (where defined), sec2A − tan2A = 1.

The value of sin A = 3/5 is given to define the angle, but the result of the identity remains constant regardless of the specific value of A.

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Alternate Method

Given: sin A = 3/5, where A is an acute angle.

Formula: sin A = Perpendicular (P) / Hypotenuse (H), sec A = H / Base (B), tan A = P / B.

⇒ Let Perpendicular (P) = 3 and Hypotenuse (H) = 5.

⇒ Base (B) = √(H2 − P2) = √(52 − 32) = √(25 − 9) = √16 = 4.

⇒ sec A = H / B = 5/4.

⇒ tan A = P / B = 3/4.

⇒ sec2A − tan2A = (5/4)2 − (3/4)2

⇒ sec2A − tan2A = 25/16 − 9/16 = 16/16 = 1.

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Identities

There are three primary Pythagorean identities: sin2θ + cos2θ = 1, 1 + tan2θ = sec2θ, and 1 + cot2θ = cosec2θ.

Acute Angle Ratios

For an acute angle (0° < A < 90°), all trigonometric ratios (sin, cos, tan, etc.) are positive.

Pythagorean Triplet

The numbers (3, 4, 5) form a Pythagorean triplet, where 32 + 42 = 52, often used in right-angled triangle problems.

questions.question: In the given figure, \(\angle PSQ = 125\) degrees and \(\angle PRT = 110\) degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of \(\angle SPR\) ?
questions.questionHtml: In the given figure, \(\angle PSQ = 125\) degrees and \(\angle PRT = 110\) degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of \(\angle SPR\)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Sum of any two exterior angles of a triangle = 180° + Interior angle of the third vertex.

∠PSQ + ∠PRT = 180° + ∠SPR

125° + 110° = 180° + ∠SPR

235° = 180° + ∠SPR

∠SPR = 235° − 180° = 55°

∴ The correct answer is 55°.

Alternate Method

Given: ∠PSQ = 125° and ∠PRT = 110°

∠PSR and ∠PSQ form a linear pair on line QR.

⇒ ∠PSR + ∠PSQ = 180°

⇒ ∠PSR + 125° = 180°

⇒ ∠PSR = 180° − 125° = 55°

Similarly, ∠PRS and ∠PRT form a linear pair on line ST.

⇒ ∠PRS + ∠PRT = 180°

⇒ ∠PRS + 110° = 180°

⇒ ∠PRS = 180° − 110° = 70°

In ΔSPR, by Angle Sum Property:

⇒ ∠SPR + ∠PSR + ∠PRS = 180°

⇒ ∠SPR + 55° + 70° = 180°

⇒ ∠SPR + 125° = 180°

⇒ ∠SPR = 180° − 125° = 55°

∴ The correct answer is 55°.

Additional Information

Exterior Angle Theorem

An exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles. For ΔSPR, ∠PSQ = ∠SPR + ∠PRS.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles of a triangle is always 180°.

Linear Pair Axiom

If a ray stands on a line, then the sum of two adjacent angles so formed is 180°.

questions.question: If a = √7 + √5 and b = √7 - √5, then a 2 + b 2 = ?
questions.questionHtml: If a = √7 + √5 and b = √7 - √5, then a<sup>2 </sup>+ b<sup>2 </sup>= ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Identify that a and b are conjugate pairs of the form (x + y) and (x − y).

Use the direct algebraic identity: a2 + b2 = (x + y)2 + (x − y)2 = 2(x2 + y2)

Here, x = √7 and y = √5.

a2 + b2 = 2[(√7)2 + (√5)2] = 2(7 + 5) = 2 × 12 = 24

∴ The correct answer is 24.

Alternate Method

Given: a = √7 + √5 and b = √7 − √5

Formula Used: (x + y)2 = x2 + y2 + 2xy and (x − y)2 = x2 + y2 − 2xy

⇒ a2 = (√7 + √5)2 = (√7)2 + (√5)2 + 2(√7 × √5)

⇒ a2 = 7 + 5 + 2√35 = 12 + 2√35

⇒ b2 = (√7 − √5)2 = (√7)2 + (√5)2 − 2(√7 × √5)

⇒ b2 = 7 + 5 − 2√35 = 12 − 2√35

⇒ a2 + b2 = (12 + 2√35) + (12 − 2√35)

⇒ a2 + b2 = 12 + 12 = 24

Therefore, the value of the expression is 24, which corresponds to option (3).

∴ The correct answer is 24.

Additional Information

Algebraic Identities for Conjugates

For any two numbers x and y: (x + y)2 + (x − y)2 = 2(x2 + y2) and (x + y)2 − (x − y)2 = 4xy.

Product of Conjugate Surds

The product of conjugate surds (√m + √n) and (√m − √n) always results in a rational number: (√m + √n)(√m − √n) = m − n.

Sum of Conjugate Surds

Adding conjugates (√m + √n) + (√m − √n) eliminates the second irrational term, resulting in 2√m.

questions.question: A shopkeeper mixes 2 kg of sugar at 40/kg with 3 kg of sugar at 50/kg. What is the price per kg of the mixture?
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper mixes 2 kg of sugar at 40/kg with 3 kg of sugar at 50/kg. What is the price per kg of the mixture?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Weighted Average Price = [(Quantity1 × Price1) + (Quantity2 × Price2)] ÷ (Total Quantity)

Average Price = (2 × 40 + 3 × 50) ÷ (2 + 3)

Average Price = (80 + 150) ÷ 5 = 230 ÷ 5 = 46

∴ The correct answer is ₹46.

Alternate Method

Given:

Quantity of Sugar A = 2 kg | Price = ₹40/kg

Quantity of Sugar B = 3 kg | Price = ₹50/kg

Calculation:

⇒ Total cost of Sugar A = 2 kg × ₹40/kg = ₹80

⇒ Total cost of Sugar B = 3 kg × ₹50/kg = ₹150

⇒ Total weight of the mixture = 2 kg + 3 kg = 5 kg

⇒ Total cost of the mixture = ₹80 + ₹150 = ₹230

⇒ Price per kg of mixture = Total Cost ÷ Total Weight

⇒ Price per kg = 230 ÷ 5 = ₹46

∴ The correct answer is ₹46.

Additional Information

Alligation Rule

It states that (Quantity of Cheaper) ÷ (Quantity of Dearer) = (Price of Dearer − Mixture Price) ÷ (Mixture Price − Price of Cheaper).

Weighted Average Concept

The average value of a set of items with different weights (quantities) is calculated by Aw = (Σ wi × xi) ÷ Σ wi.

Profit and Loss Application

If the mixture is sold at a certain profit %, first find the Cost Price (CP) of the mixture using CP = SP × 100 ÷ (100 + Profit%).

questions.question: If 60% of a number is 48, what is the number?
questions.questionHtml: If 60% of a number is 48, what is the number?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In percentage terms, 60% of the number is given as 48.

To find the 100% value (the number itself), we use the Unitary Method.

If 60% → 48, then 1% → 48 ÷ 60 = 0.8.

Therefore, 100% → 0.8 × 100 = 80.

∴ The correct answer is 80.

Alternate Method

Given:

Percentage value = 60%

Result of the percentage = 48

Formula Used:

Number = (Given Value × 100) ÷ Percentage

Calculations:

Let the required number be x.

⇒ 60% of x = 48

⇒ (60 ÷ 100) × x = 48

⇒ 0.6 × x = 48

⇒ x = 48 ÷ 0.6

⇒ x = 480 ÷ 6

⇒ x = 80

∴ The correct answer is 80.

Additional Information

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To convert a percentage into a fraction, divide the value by 100. Example: 60% = 60/100 = 3/5.

Base Number Calculation

When P% of a number is A, the number is always calculated as (A/P) × 100.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage Change = [(New Value − Original Value) ÷ Original Value] × 100.

questions.question: The ratio of the profit to the cost price of a product is 2: 7. What is the ratio of its selling price to its profit?
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of the profit to the cost price of a product is 2: 7. What is the ratio of its selling price to its profit?
questions.solution:
Let CP = 7x and Profit = 2x.

SP = CP + Profit = 7x + 2x = 9x.

Ratio of SP to Profit = SP ÷ Profit = 9x ÷ 2x = 9:2.

questions.question: \( 77 - 41 + 34 + (21 + 18) \times 2 - 55 = ? \)
questions.questionHtml: \( 77 - 41 + 34 + (21 + 18) \times 2 - 55 = ? \)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Apply BODMAS: First solve the bracket (21 + 18) = 39.

Multiply the result by 2: 39 × 2 = 78.

Combine all terms: 77 − 41 + 34 + 78 − 55 = 189 − 96 = 93.

∴ The correct answer is 93.

Alternate Method

Given expression: 77 − 41 + 34 + (21 + 18) × 2 − 55

Method: BODMAS Rule

⇒ 77 − 41 + 34 + (39) × 2 − 55 ⇒ 77 − 41 + 34 + 78 − 55 ⇒ (77 + 34 + 78) − (41 + 55) ⇒ 189 − 96 ⇒ 93

∴ The correct answer is 93.

Additional Information

BODMAS Rule

It stands for Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction. It dictates the order of operations in any mathematical expression.

Bracket Types

Brackets should be solved in the order: small brackets (), then curly brackets {}, and finally big brackets [].

Addition and Subtraction Priority

Addition and Subtraction have the same priority level and can be performed from left to right or by grouping like-signed terms.

questions.question: A sphere is completely contained within a cylinder, with the height and diameter of the cylinder matching the diameter of the sphere. Given that the volume of the sphere is 36π cm³, what is the volume of the vacant space inside the cylinder?
questions.questionHtml: A sphere is completely contained within a cylinder, with the height and diameter of the cylinder matching the diameter of the sphere. Given that the volume of the sphere is 36π cm³, what is the volume of the vacant space inside the cylinder?
questions.solution:
Let the radius of the sphere = r

(4/3)πr3 = 36π ⇒ r3 = 27 ⇒ r = 3 cm

Height of the cylinder = 2r = 6 cm

Volume of cylinder = π × 32 × 6 = 54π cm³

Vacant space = 54π − 36π = 18π cm³

questions.question: If \( x = {(\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{3})/(}{\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{3})} + ({\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{3})}/({\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{3})} \) , then the value of x is:
questions.questionHtml: If \( x = {(\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{3})/(}{\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{3})} + ({\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{3})}/({\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{3})} \), then the value of x is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For expressions of the form (√a + √b)/(√a − √b) + (√a − √b)/(√a + √b), the result is 2(a + b) / (a − b).

Here, a = 5 and b = 3.

x = 2(5 + 3) / (5 − 3) = 16 / 2 = 8.

∴ The correct answer is 8.

Alternate Method

Given: x = (√5 + √3)/(√5 − √3) + (√5 − √3)/(√5 + √3)

Formula Used: (a/b) + (c/d) = (ad + bc) / bd and (x + y)2 + (x − y)2 = 2(x2 + y2)

⇒ x = [(√5 + √3)2 + (√5 − √3)2] / [(√5 − √3)(√5 + √3)]

⇒ x = [ 2 × ( (√5)2 + (√3)2 ) ] / [ (√5)2 − (√3)2 ]

⇒ x = [ 2 × ( 5 + 3 ) ] / [ 5 − 3 ]

⇒ x = 16 / 2

⇒ x = 8

∴ The correct answer is 8.

Additional Information

Rationalization of Surds

To rationalize a denominator like (√a − √b), multiply both numerator and denominator by its conjugate (√a + √b).

Algebraic Identity 1

(a + b)2 + (a − b)2 = 2(a2 + b2). This is useful for simplifying the sum of squares of binomials.

Algebraic Identity 2

(a + b)2 − (a − b)2 = 4ab. This is used when finding the difference between squares of binomials.

questions.question: A bathroom floor measures 3.5 m in length and 2 m in width. One of its walls, which is to be tiled fully, measures 2 m in length and 2.5 m in height. If square tiles of side 25 cm are used, and an extra 12% of tiles are purchased to cover cuts and wastage, how many tiles are needed in total?
questions.questionHtml: A bathroom floor measures 3.5 m in length and 2 m in width. One of its walls, which is to be tiled fully, measures 2 m in length and 2.5 m in height. If square tiles of side 25 cm are used, and an extra 12% of tiles are purchased to cover cuts and wastage, how many tiles are needed in total?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Area of the wall to be tiled = 2 m × 2.5 m = 5 m2 = 50000 cm2.

Area of 1 square tile = 25 cm × 25 cm = 625 cm2.

Base number of tiles needed = 50000 ÷ 625 = 80 tiles.

Total tiles including 12% extra wastage = 80 × 1.12 = 89.6 tiles.

Since tiles can only be purchased in whole numbers, round up to 90.

∴ The correct answer is 90 tiles.

Alternate Method

Given:

Dimensions of the wall = 2 m (Length) and 2.5 m (Height)

Side length of one square tile = 25 cm

Extra allowance for cuts and wastage = 12%

(Note: The bathroom floor dimensions are distractor data, as only the wall is being tiled.)

Calculations:

⇒ First, convert wall dimensions from meters to centimeters (1 m = 100 cm).

⇒ Wall length = 200 cm and Wall height = 250 cm

⇒ Area of the wall = 200 × 250 = 50000 cm2

⇒ Area of 1 square tile = 25 × 25 = 625 cm2

⇒ Base number of tiles = Area of wall ÷ Area of 1 tile

⇒ Base number of tiles = 50000 ÷ 625 = 80 tiles

⇒ Additional tiles for wastage = 12% of 80 = 80 × (12 ÷ 100) = 9.6 tiles

⇒ Total tiles required = 80 + 9.6 = 89.6 tiles

⇒ Real-life items like whole tiles are rounded up to the nearest integer, which gives 90 tiles.

∴ The correct answer is 90 tiles.

Additional Information

Unit Conversion in Area

When working with mixed units, always convert the larger units to smaller units before calculating the area to avoid decimal placement errors. Remember that 1 m2 = 10000 cm2.

Wastage Allowance

In practical math problems, wastage or extra material required is always calculated on the base quantity. The final amount is mathematically formulated as: Base Quantity × (1 + Rate/100).

Handling Distractor Data

Examiners often include irrelevant information (such as the floor dimensions in this problem) to test reading comprehension and focus. Always isolate the specific subject undergoing the operation.
